title: Seminar Folio — Humanities Block-Quote Lectern
description: A graduate seminar slide organized entirely around a centered block quotation in warm cream, with small-caps course code and a single oxblood accent — modeled on the spare typographic authority of an Ivy-league seminar handout rather than a projected deck.
philosophy: This design takes its cue from the printed seminar packet: the text is the event, and the slide exists only to frame it. It refuses color variety, imagery, and any compositional device that would compete with close reading of a quoted passage. Wide vertical margins enforce a meditative pause; the oxblood accent appears exactly once, on the course code, signaling institutional gravity without ornamentation. It is made for seminar rooms of fifteen people, not auditoriums of five hundred.
goodFor: 4–8 line block quotations from primary critical-theory sources
Graduate seminars and lecture series projected at close range
Philosophy, literary criticism, and cultural-theory courses
Slides that mirror the look of a course reading packet or handout
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quantitative or empirical research presentations
Conference keynotes in large auditoriums requiring visual impact at distance
Slides juggling multiple data panels or comparative layouts
Promotional, pitch, or sales decks requiring brand energy
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Evokes the cover leaf of a printed graduate seminar packet — austere, unhurried, and typographically certain. The mood is meditative institutional authority: a single oxblood accent on the course code carries all the gravitas, while the warm cream field breathes generously around a sparse centered text stack. Compositional rhythm is strictly vertical and bilateral-symmetric, resisting lateral tension or decorative gesture. Avoid imagery, gradients, decorative rules beyond the single separator, or any element that competes with the quiet weight of the title itself.

examples.layoutNotes: Single centered column with generous outer margins of roughly 15% on each side and deep vertical padding top and bottom, enforcing the seminar-packet cover-leaf feel. Course code in small-caps sits above a hairline rule, which in turn sits above the centered title — the rule is the only structural ornament. Subtitle or term/date rests below the title at a noticeably reduced scale, completing the vertical stack. No header band, no footer bar, no page number — the bottom margin is as silent as the top.

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes a page lifted from a photocopied graduate seminar packet and projected quietly in a small room — hushed, institutional, and entirely text-driven. The block quotation occupies a centered vertical column surrounded by an expanse of warm cream, the composition meditative and portrait-like rather than scanning or horizontal. A single note of deep oxblood on the course code signals scholarly authority without any further ornamentation. Avoid imagery, decorative rules, multi-column splits, or any element that would compete with the slow, close reading of the quoted passage.
examples.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#f5f0e6"/>

  <!-- Course code, oxblood, small-caps, flush-left to quote column -->
  <text x="480" y="232" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="18" fill="#7d2a2a" letter-spacing="6" font-weight="600">
    LIT  724  ·  SEMINAR IX  ·  THE ARCHIVE AND THE WITNESS
  </text>

  <!-- Opening quotation mark, quietly oversized -->
  <text x="462" y="360" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="150" fill="#7a7468" opacity="0.55">“</text>

  <!-- Block quotation, centered in cols 3–10 (x ≈ 480 to 1440) -->
  <g font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" fill="#1e1c1a">
    <text x="480" y="398" font-size="38" font-style="italic" font-weight="400">
      <tspan x="480" dy="0">To write history, then, is not to recover the</tspan>
      <tspan x="480" dy="62">past but to inherit its silences — to sit with</tspan>
      <tspan x="480" dy="62">the document long enough that its omissions</tspan>
      <tspan x="480" dy="62">begin to speak louder than its assertions. The</tspan>
      <tspan x="480" dy="62">archive is not a vault of evidence but a</tspan>
      <tspan x="480" dy="62">grammar of power, and the historian who forgets</tspan>
      <tspan x="480" dy="62">this mistakes the catalog for the world.</tspan>
    </text>
  </g>

  <!-- Attribution, right-aligned to quote column, reduced hierarchy -->
  <text x="1440" y="850" text-anchor="end" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="20" fill="#7a7468" font-style="italic">
    — Saidiya Hartman, <tspan font-style="normal">Venus in Two Acts</tspan>, 2008, p. 11
  </text>

  <!-- Slide number, bottom-right, minimal -->
  <text x="1860" y="1030" text-anchor="end" font-family="Georgia, ui-serif, serif" font-size="13" fill="#7a7468" letter-spacing="2">07 / 24</text>
</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; the block quotation occupies cols 3–10, centered laterally with wide gutters left and right enforcing the printed-folio feel. Vertical margins are deep and approximately equal top and bottom, so the quoted passage floats in cream space rather than pressing any edge. Course code sits flush-left in small-caps above the quote's opening line, carrying the single oxblood accent; the attribution line sits directly beneath the quote's close, right-aligned to the quote column, reduced in hierarchy. Slide number anchors bottom-right at minimal scale; no header band, no rule lines, no decorative frame.
